question.prompt: A triangle and a trapezoid are equal in area. They also have the same altitude. If the base of the triangle is \(18\) inches, the median of the trapezoid is:

solutions.explanation:
The median of a trapezoid joins the midpoints of its nonparallel sides. Its length is the average of the two base lengths, so a trapezoid with median length \(m\) and altitude \(h\) has area \(mh\).

Let \(h>0\) be the common altitude, measured in inches. The triangle's area is
\[
\frac12\cdot18\cdot h=9h.
\]
Since the trapezoid has the same area, \(mh=9h\). Dividing by the positive altitude gives \(m=9\). The median is therefore \(9\) inches, choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
solutions.title: Compare the two area formulas
